channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: ‘Abre espaço para outras candidaturas’, diz Zema sobre desgaste envolvendo Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential pre-candidate, said the damage to Flávio Bolsonaro from his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro opens space for other right-wing candidacies. He stated that those associated with Vorcaro lose credibility and that the scandal may yield further developments, but affirmed he will remain in the race and supports uniting the right in a potential second-round runoff against the PT.

item.title: Nos EUA, deputados pedem investigação sobre relação de Vorcaro com a família Bolsonaro
item.description: Federal deputies allied with Lula's government urged U.S. lawmakers to investigate an alleged financial network tied to former banker Daniel Vorcaro, involving Banco Master and Reag Investimentos, which may have benefited Eduardo Bolsonaro in the United States. The request cites possible financial flows from Vorcaro's structures to U.S. companies, linked to his funding of a Bolsonaro biopic and under investigation by Brazil's Federal Police regarding the Havengate fund. Suspicions include money laundering schemes tied to the PCC and use of funds to cover Eduardo Bolsonaro's stay in the U.S.

item.title: Valdemar: “Só perderemos a eleição se formos muito incompetentes”
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL party, stated that the party and Flávio Bolsonaro will only lose the 2026 election if they are 'very incompetent'. He bases his confidence on Lula's (PT) high rejection rate as a key factor for the PL's victory in the presidential race.

item.title: Alcolumbre avalia rito inédito para PEC da escala 6×1 e governistas temem atraso
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre indicated the PEC to abolish the 6×1 work scale may be reviewed by more than one committee, potentially delaying its vote. The federal government views the proposal as strategic for the 2026 elections and fears extended debate. The proposed procedure is unprecedented, as the Senate has historically reviewed constitutional amendments only in the CCJ.

item.title: Tudo pode, menos mexer com o Pix! Flávio Bolsonaro sabe bem disso
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro attempted to distance himself from alleged Trump pressures on Pix, but his denial lacks credibility given prior lies, such as denying Vorcaro’s financing of 'Dark Horse'. The article suggests Trump used the PCC/CV 'terrorist' designation and Section 301 tariffs as pretexts for intervention, but attacking Pix would unite Brazilians across the political spectrum, directly threatening Flávio’s candidacy. Despite his evangelical voter outreach, the episode reveals that any interference with Pix would be politically suicidal due to its widespread use and popular support.

item.title: A avaliação de Romeu Zema sobre a divisão da direita nas eleições de 2026
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential pre-candidate, reiterated his criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro over his association with Daniel Vorcaro, stating that 'those who approach criminals fall greatly in my estimation,' but affirmed he will support any right-wing candidate in the second round against the PT. He noted that despite his differences with Bolsonaro and Ronaldo Caiado, the three will unite in opposition to the PT, arguing that a right with more options is beneficial for the country.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026! O FUTURO PRESIDENTE DO BRASIL Flávio Bolsonaro? Uma Virada Que Poucos Esperavam
item.description: The video discusses the possibility of Flávio Bolsonaro running for president in 2026, presenting this as an unexpected political turn in Brazil. It suggests his name is gaining traction among Bolsonaro supporters, despite initial doubts about his electoral viability.

item.title: Fux diz que Congresso não quer pagar ‘preço social’ perante eleitor e empurra decisões para o STF
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux stated that Congress often pushes difficult decisions to the Judiciary due to ideological polarization and fear of paying a 'social price' before voters. He criticized judicial activism as a reaction to legislative inaction, arguing that the STF should return to Parliament matters that belong to it. Fux emphasized that, since judges are not elected, they are compelled to decide when the Legislature remains silent.

item.title: Justiça da Colômbia proíbe candidato de usar camisa da seleção
item.description: Colombia's justice system has prohibited presidential candidate Abelardo de la Espriella from wearing the national team jersey in campaign events, ruling it compromises the neutrality of national symbols. The decision responds to complaints from the left, led by Iván Cepeda, who accuses Espriella of appropriating the jersey—a tactic popularized by Brazil's right wing. Espriella, nicknamed 'El Tigre', leads polls ahead of the June 21, 2026 runoff.

item.title: Mendonça manda retirar tornozeleira do irmão de Ciro Nogueira
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça ordered the removal of the electronic ankle monitor from Raimundo Neto e Silva Nogueira, brother of Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI), who was targeted in the fifth phase of Operation Compliance Zero investigating Banco Master frauds. The decision followed a defense request, with Mendonça concluding there is no flight risk. Raimundo denies wrongdoing, stating he served only as a formal administrator of CNLF Participações.

item.title: Veja fotos e vídeo da Marcha para Jesus 2026 em São Paulo
item.description: The 2026 March for Jesus in São Paulo gathered approximately 35,000 participants in a 3.5 km procession from Luz Station to Heróis da FEB Square, featuring gospel artists and politicians including Mayor Ricardo Nunes, Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and Attorney General Jorge Messias. In its 34th edition, the event was described as the world’s largest open-air Christian gathering, with attendees from across Brazil and countries such as the United States, Spain, Mexico, Germany, and Guatemala.

item.title: Deputados da base de Lula vão aos Estados Unidos por ajuda contra Flávio, PCC e tarifaço
item.description: Federal deputies from Lula’s base traveled to the United States to seek support from the Trump administration’s opposition against tariffs imposed on Brazilian goods, in response to the Bolsonaro family’s lobbying efforts at the White House. The initiative aims to mitigate the impact of the 'tariff barrage' on Brazil’s foreign trade, which has strained productive sectors and pressured the country’s trade balance.

item.title: O nome que virou fenômeno e lidera crescimento entre presidenciáveis no digital
item.description: Renan Santos emerged as the leading digital phenomenon in the 2026 presidential race, with a 36.89% growth in 30 days and a gain of 425,600 followers, reaching 1.58 million and a 5.29% engagement rate. Despite Renan’s rise, Lula remains the largest by volume with 14.7 million followers, while Flávio Bolsonaro is the second-largest digital force with 10.5 million followers and a gain of 337,300 accounts. Among governors, Romeu Zema lost followers and Ronaldo Caiado gained audience but with low engagement.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro adota tom eleitoral e fala em expulsar o mal durante Marcha para Jesus
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) used the March for Jesus in São Paulo to adopt an electoral tone, praying for his father Jair Bolsonaro and declaring that evil will be expelled from the Brazilian government in 2026, speaking while wrapped in an Israeli flag. He framed the political struggle as spiritual and called for the restoration of international alliances. Other figures, including Tarcísio de Freitas and Ronaldo Caiado, also spoke with emphasis on resilience and the 2026 electoral landscape.

item.title: Áudio sobre possível delação de Vorcaro vaza ao vivo na “CNN”
item.description: An audio leak during the live broadcast of CNN Brasil's Bastidores CNN captured a female voice commenting on Daniel Vorcaro's possible plea bargain, expressing hope that he had 'ratted out everyone'. The remark was made as hosts discussed Vorcaro's defense's new plea deal proposal to the Federal Police and the Attorney General's Office. The clip sparked social media speculation about the voice's origin, while CNN Brasil has not responded to Poder360's outreach attempts.

item.title: Aliados de Lula pedem aos EUA investigação sobre relação de Vorcaro com família Bolsonaro
item.description: Allies of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged U.S. Democratic lawmakers in Washington to investigate an alleged financial network linked to former banker Daniel Vorcaro, which purportedly operated in the United States to benefit members of the Bolsonaro family. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro are named as possible beneficiaries of this network, according to claims made by Lula’s allies.

item.title: A nova pesquisa Quaest sobre a eleição presidencial, após ameaça de tarifaço
item.description: The Quaest institute will release on Wednesday, June 10, a new presidential election poll based on 2,004 interviews conducted between June 5 and 8. Commissioned by Banco Genial, the survey has a two-point margin of error and is the first following Donald Trump’s threat to impose new tariffs on Brazil, one week after Flávio Bolsonaro’s visit to the White House. In the May 13 Quaest poll, Lula led with 39% and Flávio Bolsonaro with 33% in the first round, while the second-round projection showed a technical tie at 42% to 41%.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: brasileiro quer renovação, mas se sente encurralado por ‘polarização inevitável’
item.description: Brazilian independent voters desire political renewal but feel trapped by the perceived inevitability of polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, seeing little chance for a third way. Despite the weakening of both main candidates — Lulu losing momentum and Flávio facing the Master case and Bolsonarist associations — no alternative figure, such as Ronaldo Caiado, gains traction due to low name recognition and perceived electoral inviability. Many say they will vote for the 'lesser evil' or abstain entirely.

item.title: Alcolumbre quer esforço concentrado para votar nome de Benedito Gonçalves no CNJ
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre is seeking to organize a concentrated effort to vote on Benedito Gonçalves' appointment as corregedor of the CNJ, after a previous vote was canceled due to lack of quorum. The nomination faces ethical scrutiny over Gonçalves' association with a luxury event sponsored by banker Daniel Vorcaro, linked to Banco Master. Alcolumbre's approach contrasts with his earlier actions regarding Jorge Messias, whose STF nomination was blocked after alleged pressure to shield government investigations.

item.title: “Só perderemos a eleição se formos muito incompetentes”, diz Valdemar
item.description: PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto said the party will only lose the 2026 election if it is highly incompetent, citing Lula’s 48% rejection rate as an advantage. He defended Jair Bolsonaro’s government, stating that although effective governance lasted only two years due to the pandemic, it delivered strong results, and the goal is to resume economic growth and job creation. Valdemar also expressed confidence in reaching a trade agreement with the United States, arguing that both countries need each other.

item.title: Jaques Wagner associa Flávio a taxas dos EUA e cita “traição”
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for linking his visit to Donald Trump to the U.S. proposal of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, calling the act 'mean-spirited' and suggesting it amounts to 'treason'. Wagner praised Pix as a symbol of Brazilian sovereignty and innovation, claiming the U.S. and credit card companies oppose it because it is free and beneficial to the people. He concluded that Bolsonaro is unqualified to run for president in 2026 due to lack of qualifications and alleged collaboration with harmful measures against Brazil.

item.title: Elmano endossa discurso de Lula e chama Flávio de traidor da pátria
item.description: Ceará Governor Elmano de Freitas (PT) criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for President, calling him a "traitor of the homeland" for visiting Donald Trump at the White House. The remarks follow the U.S. government’s designation of Brazilian criminal factions as terrorists and proposal of new tariffs on Brazilian goods. Elmano argued that the federal government will negotiate with the U.S., while condemning Flávio’s actions as harmful to national interests.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, Tarcísio e Nunes almoçam juntos na Marcha para Jesus
item.description: PL presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro lunched with São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) during the March for Jesus. The meeting signals potential coordination among right-wing and center-right leaders ahead of the 2026 elections. No official alliance declarations were made at the event.

item.title: Flávio impõe tom eleitoral, e Messias cita Judas na Marcha para Jesus
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, adopted an electoral tone during his speech at the March for Jesus in São Paulo, asking for prayers for his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and criticizing the opposition. During the event, federal deputy Messias Messias (PL-RJ) made a biblical allusion to Judas’ betrayal to attack political adversaries, reinforcing the polarizing character of the religious gathering.

item.title: Lula diz que faltou à Marcha para Jesus para não “tirar proveito”
item.description: President Lula stated he did not attend the 2026 March for Jesus to avoid gaining political advantage from a religious event, noting he signed the law establishing the National March for Jesus Day in 2009. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the government’s main electoral opponent, attended the event and was cheered by the crowd, describing Brazil as being in a 'great spiritual war'. The march drew an estimated 35,000 participants, according to Poder360.

item.title: Crusoé: “Feminismo no Judiciário livrou a monstra”, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for presidency from the Mission party, criticized the judicial pardon granted to Monique Medeiros, mother of Henry Borel, claiming that feminism in the judiciary 'freed the monster'. He referred to the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice decision that upheld Monique's acquittal in the killing of her 4-year-old son by her former partner, Dr. Jairinho.

item.title: Crusoé: Por que Messias estava na Marcha para Jesus, segundo Messias
item.description: Jorge Messias, the Attorney General of the Union and representative of President Lula at the March for Jesus in São Paulo, stated that his presence was solely to praise and glorify God, denying any political motive.

item.title: Criadores ou replicantes?
item.description: Rafael Lazarini, entrepreneur at Live Nation and founder of Rio2C, is launching SP2B in São Paulo to explore how the boundaries between business, culture, and technology are dissolving, with growing emphasis on AI-driven content creation. The Rio2C event, held May 26–31 at Cidade das Artes, drew over 55,000 attendees, 1,732 speakers, and featured President Lula launching the Tela Brasil streaming platform, solidifying its status as Latin America’s largest creativity forum. Lazarini argues that traditional B2B and B2C frameworks no longer capture today’s reality, where culture, commerce, and public policy intertwine in hybrid events.

item.title: Novo passo em busca do público
item.description: President Lula launched the Tela Brasil streaming platform at the Rio2C event, aiming to expand access to Brazilian films. The platform debuted with 555 titles, including classics such as 'A Hora da Estrela' and 'Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol', backed by a 10.1 million reais investment. Although currently web-only, a mobile app is expected within 30 days.

item.title: Trump ataca
item.description: The article criticizes Donald Trump's actions, such as classifying domestic criminal factions as terrorists and threatening new tariffs, as part of an offensive against Brazilian sovereignty. The author argues these measures are not isolated but part of a 'liquid authoritarianism'—fragmented, seemingly legal actions that erode democracy and human rights. Trumpism is portrayed as a threat to multilateralism and national sovereignty, with dehumanizing practices toward immigrants and a hostile view of the enemy.

item.title: Terras-raras, mentes rarefeitas
item.description: The article criticizes the alleged scarcity of critical thinking in Brazil despite its abundance of rare earth minerals, using satire to denounce what the authors see as a national intelligence deficit. They propose setting targets to combat 'tupiniquim stupidity' and suggest republishing satirical works like those from MAD magazine and Stanislaw Ponte Preta to counter what they call the hyperinflation of stupidity.

item.title: A universidade sitiada
item.description: The text examines the crisis in Brazilian public universities, highlighting the tension between the university as a public good and engine of social transformation versus the claim that it is a leftist indoctrination space. This ideological conflict, fueled by liberal think tanks and extremist media since the 1980s, intensifies in the 2026 electoral context, challenging the university’s legacy as a democratic and critical institution. The strike in São Paulo universities reflects not only labor demands but a symbolic battle over the historical and social meaning of public higher education.

item.title: Tarifaço político
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro faces strong political backlash after U.S. actions threatened to impose up to 37.5% tariffs on Brazilian exports, allegedly due to his complacency during a visit to the White House. President Lula accused him of treason and of seeking foreign interference in Brazil’s internal affairs, stressing that concessions in strategic areas such as Pix, rare earths, and big tech regulation must not be made.

item.title: Na mesa de Jesus, há lugar até para Judas, diz Messias
item.description: The Attorney General of the Union, Jorge Messias, attended the March for Jesus 2026 in São Paulo alongside Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for the presidency. He stated he was sent by President Lula to praise and worship God, rejecting the notion of a political rally at the event and emphasizing that Jesus’ table welcomes all, even Judas, without segregation.

item.title: Governo Lula diz que argumentos dos EUA para tarifas são ilegítimos
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira rejected the U.S. justification for imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, calling the arguments illegitimate. He emphasized Brazil’s interest in continuing dialogue with the U.S. following the early release of Section 301 investigation reports, which accused Brazil of unfair trade practices including Pix usage, weak intellectual property protection, corruption, and deforestation. The proposed tariffs would affect a broad range of Brazilian exports, excluding certain agricultural, aerospace, and pharmaceutical products.

item.title: Marcha para Jesus reúne cerca de 35.000 pessoas em São Paulo
item.description: The 2026 March for Jesus gathered approximately 35,000 people on Estado Avenue in São Paulo, with the area measured at 7,292.19 m² using drone imagery and Google Earth. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) attended, was cheered, and expressed support for his father, Jair Bolsonaro, describing Brazil as engaged in a 'great spiritual war'. Attorney General Jorge Messias also participated but remained isolated on the sound truck, stressing the event's sole purpose was to worship Jesus without political division. President Lula did not attend, stating he avoids religious events during election periods to avoid appearing opportunistic.

item.title: Pauta antifacção consolida Flávio como presidenciável com mais engajamento nas redes
item.description: The federal government's designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations boosted Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) as the presidential candidate with the highest social media engagement in May, according to a DSC Lab survey. The move reinforced his central role in the public security debate and strengthened his conservative electoral base.

item.title: Caiado viraliza com bronca em podcaster por discurso contra vacinas
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) went viral after confronting podcaster Felipe Sestaro during an IronTalks interview, defending Covid-19 vaccines based on the Hippocratic Oath. Caiado emphasized that saving lives is the core principle of medicine, criticizing the interviewer's anti-vaccine stance. The video compilation gained widespread traction on social media.

item.title: Violência lidera preocupações do eleitorado para 2026
item.description: Violence and insecurity are the top concerns of Brazilian voters ahead of the 2026 elections, with 96.2% reporting fear related to crime. The issue transcends ideology, leading among Lula supporters (36%), independents (31%), and right-wing voters, indicating cross-partisan mobilization potential. The public strongly supports strengthening security institutions — such as prosecuting criminals (73%), police body cameras (82%), and enforcing existing laws (55%) — while rejecting punitive rhetoric like 'a good criminal is a dead one' (20%).

item.title: Liderados por Janones, lulistas dizem defender Pix em Washington
item.description: Left-wing deputies André Janones, Jandira Feghali, Pedro Campos and Pedro Uczai traveled to Washington D.C. to defend Brazil’s Pix payment system, claiming they aim to expose what they see as Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s inconsistencies on the issue while in the United States.

item.title: Mendonça arquiva ação do PT por vídeo de deputado em apoio a Flávio
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça dismissed a petition by the Santa Catarina PT seeking to fine state deputy Antídio Lunelli for affixing a pro-Flávio Bolsonaro sticker on his car, which the party argued constituted premature electioneering. The minister ruled that such electoral violation claims must be filed by national party directories, not state-level ones, rendering the PT-SC petition inadmissible. Lunelli hailed the decision as a defense of free expression, while the PT has not responded to requests for comment.

item.title: Kassio assume no TSE ações sobre ‘Dark Horse’ e pesquisa que cita áudio de Flávio
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques has been appointed rapporteur for three actions concerning the film 'Dark Horse' and the AtlasIntel poll referencing audio of Flávio Bolsonaro. The cases allege economic and political abuse in the film's financing and improper voter influence in the poll, which showed Flávio at 41.8% versus Lula's 48.9% in a hypothetical runoff. Nunes Marques, along with André Mendonça and Estela Aranha, forms the trio tasked with reviewing electoral propaganda actions during the 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Rui Costa chama família Bolsonaro de “traidores da pátria”
item.description: Rui Costa, PT-BA’s Senate pre-candidate, accused Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro of being 'traitors of the homeland' for allegedly supporting the U.S. proposal to impose 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods and seeking to dismantle Brazil’s Pix payment system. He also criticized Bahian opposition politicians for staying silent on the issue, saying the people of Bahia want to know their stance.

item.title: Um ambiente acolhedor que transforma vidas
item.description: The TEA Paulista Center, inaugurated on June 4, 2025, by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, provides specialized care, support, and inclusion services for autistic individuals and their families. In its first year, it delivered nearly 4,000 attendances and over 700 workshops, fostering autonomy, social inclusion, and professional training, becoming a benchmark for disability inclusion in São Paulo state.

item.title: Crusoé: A religiosidade seletiva de Lula
item.description: The article claims that Lula's participation in religious events is driven solely by his desire for re-election, not by genuine faith, as he allegedly lacks religiosity. His stance is described as selective and contradictory, shaped by electoral interests. The piece criticizes the instrumentalization of religion as a political strategy.

item.title: Crusoé: “Não abriremos mão”, diz Caiado sobre o Pix
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) defended the Pix payment system in an interview with Crusoé, stating he will not abandon it. His remarks come in response to the U.S. Trade Representative's proposal to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian imports, citing alleged unfair practices by the Brazilian government.

item.title: ‘Meu filho, para eles, é um caso perdido’, diz mãe de menino com câncer, sobre governo Lula
item.description: The mother of 8-year-old Luís Benke accuses the Lula government of neglecting to help bring her son, hospitalized in Lisbon with cancer metastasis, back to Brazil for treatment, calling him a 'lost cause'. She says she has contacted all possible authorities without response, while the repatriation cost is estimated at R$1.2 million. Santa Catarina’s government has sued the federal government to act, which has also remained silent.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest mostra disputa Lula x Flávio após novo tarifaço de Trump
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll, set for release starting June 10, will assess whether Lula’s lead over Flávio Bolsonaro has solidified following the audio scandal with Daniel Vorcaro and rising Brazil-U.S. tensions. The survey will examine Flávio’s erosion among moderate and independent voters, as well as the potential for a right-wing third-way alternative. It will be the institute’s first poll after a series of surveys showed fluctuating margins between the two main candidates.

item.title: Kássio relatará ações no TSE sobre dinheiro de Vorcaro para filme de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the TSE, will serve as rapporteur for three representations regarding the film 'Dark Horse', financed by Daniel Vorcaro with at least 61 million reais. The actions include a PL challenge against an AtlasIntel poll, a PT request to block the film's exhibition as parallel propaganda, and a complaint alleging economic and political abuse in its funding. The case is tied to the 2026 elections and raises concerns about private resource use in electoral campaigns.

item.title: Lula justifica ausência na Marcha para Jesus com a pior desculpa possível
item.description: President Lula once again failed to attend the March for Jesus, a religious event he himself sanctioned in 2009. His absence was justified by him with an explanation critics deemed weak, while Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias represented him at the event and later posted a video on social media.
